name: zermatt-window
description: A 64×64 rectangle of real SRTM1 data over Zermatt village, cut byte-for-byte out of N46E007. Committed as the offline evidence that this mirror is void-filled: the valley floor reads a real elevation here, not the −32768 void marker.

source.dataset: SRTM1 (1 arc-second) via the AWS elevation-tiles-prod "skadi" mirror
source.license: SRTM is public domain (NASA/USGS); the AWS mirror is a public dataset.

statistics.note: voidSamples is 0 because the skadi mirror is void-filled — verified across N45E007, N46E007, N27E086, N28E086 (0 voids in 51 868 804 samples). The void code path is covered by the synthetic fixtures instead.

accuracyCaveat: SRTM under-reads AND displaces sharp summits. In N45E007 the Matterhorn tops out at 4230 m against a surveyed 4478 m, and that posting sits ~320 m WSW of the surveyed summit position (which itself reads 3567 m, already down the east side); Dent d'Hérens 3835 vs 4171 m; the broad Grand Combin 4287 vs 4314 m. Use these tiles for the terrain horizon; take summit heights from the peak database's ele tag.
